title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: Ray’s car averages \(40\) miles per gallon of gasoline, and Tom’s car averages \(10\) miles per gallon of gasoline. Ray and Tom each drive the same number of miles. What is the cars’ combined rate of miles per gallon of gasoline?

solutions.text: If each drives \(D\) miles, together they cover \(2D\) miles using \(\dfrac{D}{40}+\dfrac{D}{10} = \dfrac{D}{8}\) gallons. The combined rate is \(\dfrac{2D}{\frac{D}{8}} = 16\) miles per gallon. Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Combined mileage is total miles divided by total gallons, not the average of the two rates
If each drives \(D\) miles, the gallons used are \(\dfrac{D}{40}\) and \(\dfrac{D}{10}\)
